clue.text: Briefcase for an agriculturalist?

parts.note: a briefcase is a little container for papers; read as a modest container, it also names someone who farms a few acres

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what sort of bag a farmer carries to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests luggage; the trick is to read 'briefcase' as a little case, a small thing that holds, which turns into a small-scale farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person working a small plot of farmland in Britain is called by this term, so it fits an agriculturalist.

clue.text: Proposes to give yours truly the answer

parts.note: a stock phrase the speaker uses for themselves, so it gives ME

explanation.surface: A suitor offers themselves as the reply to a question.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend or plan something is to propose it, a verb sense shared by both words.

clue.text: They want tenants with erudition

definitions.meaning: landlords who let property want tenants, so they are people who let
a person of learning is said to be a man or woman of ...

explanation.surface: Landlords seek lodgers who are well read.
explanation.definitionFit: People who let rooms want tenants, and learning or literary scholarship is also called by this word.

clue.text: Needing to make crone consume French wine

indicators.note: the old woman consumes, taking the wine into her middle

parts.note: a crone is an ugly old woman, a hag
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: An old woman has to drink a glass of French red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing' stands for the answer only in a phrase like 'having to make', so the swap works with the 'to' that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'having to go' the word means needing or being obliged to, so the two are interchangeable before 'to'.

clue.text: High-flier means to come down by train

parts.note: an aircraft comes down when it lands
travelling by train is travelling by rail

explanation.surface: A jet-setting executive arrives by train instead of flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' suggests a jet-setter, but it is a bird; 'means' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The corncrake, a bird, goes by this other name; a bird is a flier, made 'high' for the surface.

clue.text: Book up! I've found it to be quite moving

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word for book is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a novel and declares it very touching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book up!' reads as an exclamation about reservations; in a down clue 'up' turns the book word to EMOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emotive stirs the feelings, which is what a touching or stirring thing does.

clue.text: Made andrea healthy? Yes, indeed!

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a treatment restored Andrea to health and is told emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' rearranges the thirteen letters of ANDREA HEALTHY; the whole clue also describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means robust and vigorous, exactly what someone restored to full health is.

clue.text: Gloomy, like the play's producer?

definitions.meaning: a dull, cloudy sky is gloomy
a producer is in charge of, so above, the actors in a show

explanation.surface: A theatre producer is in low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: the producer is over the cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A clouded sky is dull and dark, and a producer stands over the troupe of actors.

clue.text: Deliver French coffee to a modest diner

parts.note: to deliver goods is to carry or transport them
cafe is the French word for coffee

explanation.surface: Someone brings a French coffee to a humble customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diner' looks like a person eating, but it is a roadside eatery; a TRANSPORT CAFE is a cheap British roadside restaurant for lorry drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap roadside eating place used by lorry drivers in Britain is a humble restaurant.

clue.text: Tailor makes a lawyer take exercise

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US lawyer
PT is physical training, school exercise

explanation.surface: A clothier persuades an attorney to work out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' looks like a noun, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to modify it to suit, a synonym of adjust.

clue.text: Vehicle insurance needed to go round stylish Canadian city

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: the insurance goes round, enclosing the letter for stylish

parts.note: insurance is cover against loss
U means upper-class, so smart or stylish

explanation.surface: A van owner needs a policy before driving a fashionable route round town.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class, hence smart or stylish, is an old crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pacific port in British Columbia, it is one of the largest urban centres in Canada.

clue.text: Initially expatriate a more inflexible Asian

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word expatriate is taken

parts.note: sterner means stricter, more unbending

explanation.surface: An expatriate becomes harder in attitude than before.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the East, from Asia, is described with this word.

clue.text: Pakistani cricketer sees many in Persia

indicators.note: the letter for many goes in the country name

parts.note: Persia is the old name for Iran
M, the Roman thousand, stands for a large number

explanation.surface: A Pakistani sportsman notices crowds in Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: Imran Khan was a famous Pakistan cricket captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Imran Khan captained Pakistan at cricket and won the 1992 World Cup.

clue.text: He likes life in the raw

definitions.text: He likes life in the raw

parts.words: He likes life in the raw
parts.note: 'in the raw' sounds like rough living, but it also means naked

explanation.surface: A rugged man enjoys an unvarnished, primitive existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who prefers going without clothes, being naked, lives 'in the raw'.

clue.text: I told ray off for tending to procrastinate

indicators.note: off means the letters are wrong or awry, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told Ray to stop putting things off.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilatory person is slow and delaying, inclined to put things off.

clue.text: A gas heater requires moisture

parts.note: a fire heats a room
damp is moisture

explanation.surface: A gas heater needs some humidity to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas heater' reads as one appliance; split it, 'A gas' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane found in coal mines, explosive when mixed with air, is a gas.

clue.text: Relief organisation makes Labourite furious

parts.note: a left-winger, a Labour Party supporter, is called a red
cross means angry

explanation.surface: A Labour member is enraged.
explanation.walkthrough: The British Labour Party is left-wing, hence RED.
explanation.definitionFit: The international humanitarian movement that gives aid in disasters is a relief organisation.

clue.text: Basilica due to be consecrated

parts.note: a basilica was originally a Roman public hall
money due is owed

explanation.surface: A great church is about to be blessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basilica' suggests a church, fitting the surface, but it is the Roman sense, a large hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed ground is holy, made sacred by blessing.

clue.text: Playing whilst travelling by coach

definitions.meaning: an actor who is playing is performing before an audience
riding in an old horse-drawn coach, a stage

explanation.surface: An actor performs while on a coach trip.
explanation.walkthrough: A stage, or stagecoach, was a horse-drawn coach, so a passenger is on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors performing are in front of the audience, and a passenger rides on a stagecoach.

clue.text: He reads part of the collect orthodox churches prescribe

indicators.note: only a part of the two words is taken, the run lying across them

explanation.surface: A reader recites a prayer that Orthodox churches require.
explanation.walkthrough: A collect is a short church prayer; the reader fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A lector is a person who reads lessons aloud in a church service.

clue.text: Church section upset by member rejecting gospel

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the church part is turned upside down

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

indicators.note: rejecting turns the limb back on itself

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member

explanation.surface: Part of the congregation is offended when a member turns down the Gospel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NAVE into EVAN; 'rejecting' turns LEG into GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an old word for the good news, the Christian message.

clue.text: Immoral person might get on

parts.note: 'get on' reads as getting along, but in slang to get it on is to have sex, which a promiscuous person might do readily

explanation.surface: A bad character could still be good company.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose, promiscuous person is called by this old noun, sexually unrestrained.

clue.text: One beset by workers who are hostile

indicators.note: the one is surrounded, beset, by the insects

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An employee is surrounded by unfriendly colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Antis are people opposed to something, so they are hostile to it.

clue.text: Cleaner goes to a court sitting by coach

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a British cleaning lady
banc is the bench of judges, a court sitting in full

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady travels to a court hearing by coach.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR is a British cleaning woman; a CHARABANC was an early motor coach for outings.
explanation.definitionFit: An old open motor bus for day trips is a kind of coach.

clue.text: High up in an attic

parts.note: the indefinite article, a
a loft is an attic

explanation.surface: Something is stored high up under the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft means overhead, in the air, raised high.

clue.text: Move round for a complete change

definitions.meaning: a reversal of opinion or policy

explanation.surface: A turn of direction brings a total transformation.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning to face the other way is a physical reversal, and a U-turn in policy is a reversal of view.

clue.text: Cease to function and leave

definitions.meaning: a lamp or alarm stops working or goes dead

explanation.surface: A machine breaks down and someone walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights or a heating system that switch off stop working, and a person who departs sets out, both senses of this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Only a priest displayed character

indicators.note: the words are displayed in a new arrangement, rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone cleric revealed his nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's character is their individual nature and temperament.
